Sample.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/6] Findings from the current study with a diverse group of adolescents (52% ethnic minority) demonstrate that PTA was an effective program for decreasing depression symptoms when compared to a control group receiving limited non-specific support.
Sample.warning: N_total not found in this section.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/6] PTA was developed specifically for early adolescents using age-appropriate curriculum material, and used skills-based training and psychoeducation to parents via workshops and home visits, in addition to the student groups.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/7/Text/5] Other limitations of the current study include lack of diagnostic data regarding onset of depressive episodes or disorder, and examination of outcomes at post-treatment only.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/7] In the current study, we found program effects for youth-reported depression outcomes but not those reported by parents or teachers. [/page/7/Text/5] Moreover, despite gathering outcome data from multiple informants including parents and teachers, the fact that significant group differences emerged only for youth-reported outcomes somewhat limits the robustness of the findings. [/page/6/Text/9] Youth-reported personal adjustment indicated advantages of PTA in sense of inadequacy and self-esteem... [/page/7/Text/4] We did find a beneficial effect of PTA on parent-reported social skills, although evidence suggested no effect for other aspects of interpersonal functioning.
